Thanks [@Shankar Warang](/edgeware/account/jA7pLH65zgRNA4UgwqHEWWRxTgg51wuAUgfzmZoYWM2dMVS) -  i didn't know some of this.

In the end we have spoken about showing **commitment **to individuals and teams - **commitment is shown**, like **trust is earned not bought**. 

The DTrade team have made a decision in the interests of their product and their investors and so they are looking at the available information and are focused on launching where they think they will have the greatest chance of success. 

There is no loyalty to Edgeware - but that is unfortunately the transactional nature of most business. 

In the end we can only wish them well and both learn from the experience. 

We should be no less supportive of new people and projects who arrive at Edgeware's door - the right people will stay and those who see brighter lights elsewhere will leave. C'est la vie.

[@rich](/edgeware/account/5E5HAQf3Afbw5Z8gNgS3MNA3jBA41v2XhYKctPUtf9GYq5zS) I wouldn't say "**DTrade has never been an Edgeware project"**. 

As a treasury funded agency member I personally facilitated the following things:
1. Introducing dTrade to Biconomy for integrating meta-tx which dTrade now advertise as their own feature "[Zero gas fees sponsored by dTrade](https://twitter.com/dtradeorg/status/1420415072841650176?s=20)"! 
- Biconomy got funded from Edgeware Treasury and they are helping all Edgeware Ecosystem projects to integrate meta-txs. 
- Biconomy team spent considerable time with the dTrade team testing on Edgeware. 
2. The hiring of Community Managers for dTrade.
- I worked with Zabi on this.
- The CMs prepared full-fledged FAQs and were preparing several resources but then they after almost a month were told that dTrade is looking for someone who can speak Mandarin or Korean. 
- Those CMs were not incentivized at all for their contribution. 
3. Business Development for dTrade:
- John Wang from dTrade reached out to me for help with partnerships.
- We together listed down potential stakeholders and designed priority for further Business Development (in which I wasn't involved).


So dTrade did benefit indirectly from Edgeware Treasury resources.

But on the other hand, as [@Zabi - dTrade](/ethereum/account/0x94279E2E8fe469DD4685D1665245099Fe855E2fB) mentioned dTrade did contribute several things to Edgeware like beresheet faucet, integrated yieldscan and ink! tutorial. One more thing worth mentioning is Humza from dTrade lead Edgeware's DeFi Working Group and DeFi WG Calls. So it was a mutual relationship and dTrade **was **a part of the Edgeware Ecosystem despite not being directly funded by Edgeware Treasury.
As many of dTrade's investors pressured them to deploy on the earliest parachains, it makes sense for them to pursue a different path based on speculation backed by Kusama auctions' results. Wishing dTrade team good luck for their launch.

Thanks for the update [@Zabi](/edgeware/account/5CJdYxYeNk3bXdswVs7CQwbNdwAPnwrpu4dx75CLYN3cyQcM) and best of luck to you with your endeavours. 

Would rather avoid anymore mud slinging - if Dtrade team have made a decision to launch on another chain then that’s fair and their decision. 

**It it worth reiterating that DTrade has never been an Edgeware project. **

The chain is _permissionless_ - meaning none of us have control over who deploys, where we do have agency is with the _permissioned_ community fund, where we are more closely aligned with contributors and teams who explicitly receive funds for projects that the Edgeware community deems valuable.

1. The permissionless part is analogous to Ethereum - a generic, smart contract platform, where anyone can deploy, anything at anytime. 
2. The permissioned part is novel and native to our Substrate base and includes a few complimentary components, namely the treasury, governance systems and this interface. 


The second part is definitively where the community has an ability to express and debate and implement its shared voice by the virtue of anyone being able to put forward and propose changes to the overall system and to projects we wish to fund.

[@Zabi](/edgeware/account/5CJdYxYeNk3bXdswVs7CQwbNdwAPnwrpu4dx75CLYN3cyQcM) noted that they still hold 2.5m EDG from the staking UI work - something that was community funded. 

If DTrade had been community funded and then deployed first on other chains or moved away from alignment with Edgeware would then have cause to be upset, but they didn't - in the end the timing of the Staking UI and development of DTrade plus Commonwealth's involvement was perhaps poorly communicated, but in the end we get nowhere by just rehashing all of this stuff.

Who knows what the future holds, but things tend to join up in weird ways and so there will be a place for the Dtrade team if they decide to return and put forward a funding proposal to the community.

Despite the negativity of some, we the EDG community have come a long way since launch and are gradually figuring out our own culture and strategy with [Kabocha](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1415-kabocha-kab-canarynet-proposal) / [multi chain incubator](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1415-kabocha-kab-canarynet-proposal) that potentially takes a stake in many chains. 

Personally I have never been more excited about Edgeware's future - sure it will be a bit chaotic, messy, ill-defined and weird in these early stages, but at least we can be confident that we are now on a track to creating something genuinely new - experimenting and playing with the possibilities this brave new world affords.

This whole process once again reinforces EDG as one of the most experienced projects when it comes to truly decentralised on-chain governance - remember every Substrate chain launching has all of this to come - to think that they will just magically develop this experience is naive. 

Often you learn more when things don’t work out as intended as you do when your plan works perfectly*

*it never does.

The issued grant amounts succeeded in allowing Seedcode to pay its employees to work on everything that was delivered as detailed by [@Zabi - dTrade](/ethereum/account/0x94279E2E8fe469DD4685D1665245099Fe855E2fB) 's post and likely fell short tremenously given the time they ended up allocating in the end. It consists of a tremendous amount of work. If you hate developers this much to keep dragging this out on delivery when no final delivery payment was collected, I personally am not interested to hear your thoughts much further.

**The dev time allocated to this project was massively under-estimated and massively over-delivered.**
Whether people want to believe us or not and granted there were hiccups with shifting developers on Seedcode's side due to individual personal reasons during COVID, Seedcode dedicated a tremendous amount of developer time than was possibly covered in costs with the ~3ish million EDG at the time.

We worked together on the staking UI, developing and QA'ing it for over 8 months. We developed against (a) moving designs and (b) moving architectures of the Commonwealth interface. The grant did not include capacity for other Commonwealth Labs members to integrate, QA, and update designs of these components over time and ultimately myself nor Seedcode possessed merge power over the Commonwealth Interface. Nonetheless, people in CW Labs DID contribute QA time and design time. In the end as [@Zabi - dTrade](/ethereum/account/0x94279E2E8fe469DD4685D1665245099Fe855E2fB) has pointed out in his post, the work was done up to a point in which it made absolutely no sense to integrate and finish. That developer time was a sunk cost past the last grant payment.

Yes some grants fail, I'm shocked.

**dTrade & Seedcode & this grant**
Since I'm not spending time reading these threads all the time, it's worth setting the record straight. I did not work on dTrade with funds from this grant, I worked on Staking UI. You can check my Github commits, you can check Seedcode developers commits. You can check the eventual dTrade Github repo. I have contributed to the bridge at times far outside the scope of this staking UI project. Not sure why there's so much misinformation in this thread. Some of y'all are really mad and you just can't seem to get over yourselves.

EDIT: Mistaken that all of Seedcode's EDG was sold, my mistake (I'm not reading everything here)

body:
The staking UI was proposed to address one main problem, which is that it was impossible to view staking yield in mid/late 2020.

That was resolved by Parity when they made substantial changes to the Substrate runtime. Afterwards even remz commented that it was likely not worth it to finish the Staking UI work in Commonwealth, and in addition said that he did not consider dTrade a valuable or successful project (this was after they had raised their seed funding from Polychain).

---

This highlights the importance of maintaining alignment across all parties working on the network.

For dTrade close alignment would not look like owning a percentage of EDG - as a DeFi protocol they care about liquidity, and participation from market makers, traders, and institutions, (eg prime brokers who can maintain a steady funding rate).

In the last few months Edgeware has gone in a different direction -- the parabridge strategy would make EDG less aligned with DOT and deter protocols who want to be major Polkadot ecosystem players. Across all of this, dTrade was not consulted, and when the possibility that they would move to another network was raised, that was also dismissed by several key community members.

This is fine as long as the community is aware that these strategic decisions do have implications for the kind of projects that can build and launch on Edgeware, and who would stay in the community or join vs leaving. For now, EDG definitely seems like a better place for projects who are aligned with broad decentralization and that could be a strong community in its own right.

**P.S. **We hold over 84% of the 2.275m EDG we got. Can't speak to Drew's .975m EDG portion. None of the EDG we sold is from the second grant.

We sold our EDG from the first grant (that was marked completed by you, the community and CW), but actually ended up buying it back at a higher price instead of cashing it out from the exchange.

Yea that’s exactly how a dev shop works — it does multiple projects at the same time. It’s the same with all of the other clients Seedcode has — there’s no exclusivity and devs have to move from project to project, that’s completely normal for the industry. Milestone 1 was completed on time (completion was confirmed by CW and by yourself Remz before you funded the next milestone). Seedcode also completed Milestone 2 but ran into technical challenges with Milestone 3 that required the support of Commonwealth. There was a fair bit of backend work involved and we spent months fixing the archival node issue with Commonwealth.  We decided with Drew and Commonwealth not apply for the remaining 35% of the grant (funds for that are still in the treasury as was confirmed in the final community update [https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1160-staking-ui-final-community-update](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1160-staking-ui-final-community-update) ) — especially because the work we were doing was very low priority for Edgeware and working on something like the bridge was a far more important task.

The additional things — the faucet, yieldscan, the ink! tutorial, even the bridge UI were all not needed for dTrade. We did them for Edgeware.

The additional things — the faucet, yieldscan, the ink! tutorial, even the bridge UI were all not needed for dTrade. We did them for Edgeware.

**Since you seemed to have missed the update from 8 months ago -- I will post it again here: **

We officially started development on Staking UI in the last week of July and completed everything (within the estimated timeline) except the archival node related task for reasons mentioned in point 6 below, and commonwealth is supporting us to solve those issues. Almost all tickets were completed 6 weeks ago: [https://github.com/orgs/hicommonwealth/projects/4](https://github.com/orgs/hicommonwealth/projects/4)

Staking UI Updates & Info
Reference: [https://github.com/orgs/hicommonwealth/projects/4](https://github.com/orgs/hicommonwealth/projects/4)
**1) Validators Page: (Merged in Staking UI)**
- Moved API calls for fetching data from front-end to backend.Implemented the following APIs to retrieve the information needed to be shown on the UI:The /getValidatorsNamesAndAddresses route fetches the address and names of the validator (active, waiting) from the Valdators table
- /getValidatorDetails takes a list of addresses of validators as input and returns the following details: **totalStake**, **ownStake**, **othersStake**, **commission**, **APR, 30 day rewards count, 30 day slashes count, 30 day offenses count.** The route fetches all this data from the HistoricalValidatorStatistics table
- The /getGlobalStatistics route is responsible for fetching and computing stats to be shown on the header of the validators page. These stats include: **numOfValidators, numOfWaitingValidators, totalEras, totalSession, lastBlock#, totalStakedAmount, stakedPercent, estimatedAPR.** All the data is fetched from the chain except **estimatedAPR**. This is computed on every API call using the APR of validators stored in HistoricalValidatorStatistics
- Implemented search functionality to search validators using their name or address. For every keystroke, the list of validators is matched against the input string and the validators in the list are shown/hidden if the search string matches the name/address of the validator
- Paginated the validator view to retrieve data for 20 validators at a time

**2) Validator Details Page: (Merged in Staking UI)**
- Implemented the following APIs:The /getValidatorHeaderStats route returns the following details that are displayed in header of the page: APR, uptime%, rewards (count, value), slashes (count, value) and offenses (count). APR, uptime% and 30 days values are fetched from HistoricalValidatorStatistics while the values for rewards, slashes and offenses since the birth of the validator are fetched from the chain-events table using the /getRewards , /getSlashes and /getOffences routes.The /getRewards route fetches rewards earned by the validator over time (block)
- The /getSlashes route gets slashes for validators over time (block)
- The /getOffences route gets offenses
- The /getNominatorsOverTime route returns the number of nominators a validator has over time (block)
- The /getTotalStakeOverTime route returns the total stake of the validator over time (block)
- The /getOwnStakeOverTime route returns the own stake of a validator over time (block)
- The /getOtherStakeOverTime route returns others stake over time
- The /getNominatorsOverTime route returns the number of nominators over time
- ChartJs is used for creating the graphs. Graphs show the block number over the x-axis and values (in million, percentage or count) on the y-axis. For every block number we have a reward, slash, offense, etc. The graphs show data bucket-wise and we have defined a bucket size of 27000 blocks, showing 8 buckets on the graph. For every bucket the average of the value over the bucket is plotted on the graph.

**3) Manage Staking UI (Merged in Staking UI)**
**4) Calculator UI: (Merged in Staking UI)**
- UI to compute the return on investmentThe UI pulls CurrentStakingPercentage, CurrentSupplyOfTokens from the chain.
- For every chain, the following details are needed to provide estimates: ideal staking rate, ideal interest rate, min inflation rate, max inflation rate and decay rate. For now fetched these numbers form [lib.rs](<[http://lib.rs>)](http://lib.rs>)) and hardcoded in the config for calculator UI but in the future it would be great if we can pull all this data from an api.
- Created an API for pulling USD prices of the selected currency. Actually using the mxc api underneath, but for some reason the API didn't seem to work when invoked on front-end so invoked this api using axios on backend.
- Formulae used for computation of estimated earning, network share and adjusted reward rate could be found [here.](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1VoQbTfEZK8fPtwfhEIPYnPvw16iMI4A2y_VCuQKt2RQ/edit#gid=100091857)

**5) Event Handlers: (Merged in Staking UI)**
- New Session Event Handler: Executes on a new session event. Updates the Validators table with new validators. Updates the HistoricalValidatorStatistics table replicating the last record of each validator and then updating their exposureSlashes Event Handler: Executes on a slash event. Creates a new entry in HistoricalValidatorStatistics for the validator being slashed by replicating their last record of the db. It updates the exposure and **slashesStats** (count. sum, avg). If a nominator is being slashed, then the record of its validator is updated. One case not handled at the moment is what if the nominator being slashed is nominating multiple validators - in such a case which validator should have their exposure updated?
- Bond/Unbond Event Handler: Executes on bond and unbond events. It updates the exposure of the validator with the amount bonded or unbonded
- SomeOffline Event Handler: Executes when an offline event occurs. It replicates the last record of the validators in someOffline event and decreases their uptime%.
- All Good Event Handler: Executes when the all good event triggers. In this case the uptime% of the validators is incremented!
- Offence Event Handler: Replicates the last record of the validator from the db and updates their offenceStats.
- Rewards Event Handler: Triggers when a reward event is fired! For each validator who receives the reward, it updates their exposure if the destination is staking. It also recomputes the APR of the validator who received the reward. APR is computed based on the rewards received by the validator in last 30 days.
- Heartbeat Handler: Writes the address of the person who sent the heartbeat to the console

**6) Archival Node: (In Progress)**
- This is still not finished because of which we are unable to run our event handlers through all the past events and build the validators_historical_tableWith the support of Commonwealth, here are all the things we have attempted to resolve this issue:October 7-15: Resolving chain-event spec mismatch
- October 12-14: Edgeware-node was not building anymore on master branch due to changes pushed to master branch → resolved by overriding to 2020-08-20 and downgrading rust
- October 19: Bumped up the chain-events version to resolve a new error
- October 24: Got the chain-events listener running but it could only listen to the latest event. We then attempted to fully sync the archival node before running the chain-events listener. But were still unable to link the chain-events master branch with the commonwealth master branch. This linking is necessary because the event handlers are in the CW repo so in order to test them, we need to evaluate the handlers against the events being caught by the chain-events listener.
- November 17: Syncing the archival node completely and then running the archival node still only gave us just the latest events and no past events. We decided with Commonwealth to then try and run a poller to listen to past events instead of a subscriber.
- Today: Running the poller-batch script to fetch past events did not work. We will be writing a wrapper script tomorrow to attempt another approach.

body: thank you Remz for such a summary...if this is the case, well....certainly it doesn't leave a positive impression...

I feel like I should clarify some of the information I discussed already on matrix, to answer some of the claims above:

**Fact 1:** The council funded Seedcode for a staking UI on the 24th of May 2020. Here is [the transaction](https://edgeware.subscan.io/treasury/6), and [another one](https://edgeware.subscan.io/treasury/8) in July.

The product should have been delivered in August.

I feel like I should clarify some of the information I discussed already on matrix, to answer some of the claims above:

**Fact 1:** The council funded Seedcode for a staking UI on the 24th of May 2020. Here is [the transaction](https://edgeware.subscan.io/treasury/6), and [another one](https://edgeware.subscan.io/treasury/8) in July. 

**Fact 2:** The team for the staking included Rabeel, Yameen, Drew as per [the original proposal](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/454-staking-ui-grant-proposal-draft). All those are part of dTrade.
The product should have been delivered in August. 

**Fact 3: **We had no update after the conversation in July, and no proof that any work had been performed further. Questions had been raised during community calls, but Drew answered vaguely that he was "sorry it was taking so long". The official answer from [this thread](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1160-staking-ui-final-community-update) was sent one year after the original funding. The dates could be checked easily.

**Fact 4:** dTrade has been developed and announced within that period.

So from those facts, something very simple is to be concluded: at least the 3 members mentioned above worked on dTrade with the funding of the treasury in the meantime instead of completing their contract. 
Since this is an onchain contract, there is little that can be done to enforce the use of the resources if the contractor is dishonest. But real contractor or employment agreements prevent the focus on competitive or related business during the time of the contract. So this point has been violated by at least 3 members. There is unfortunately little that Edgeware can do about it, and this is more something that the investors in dTrade should have cared about. It is customary to ask for disclosure of other obligations. Different ones care about different things, and it seems this part did not matter for many of them.

So the description of Shankar is perfectly accurate about the funding. He never mentioned that the treasury funded dTrade under its name. 
What we see above though is that the treasury funded seedcode/Drew to work on Edgeware and that seedcode/Drew created and launched dTrade instead with the funding during the contract period without fulfilling it. Eventually the delivery happened long after dTrade started, and something unmergeable and of poor quality (according to the thread above) was quickly thrown through. This is not really acceptable.

Now to answer the different points of Zabi:
> Both the Edgeware lead developer and Seedcode received this grant, and both decided it did not make sense to complete parts of the third milestone

This is a decentralized community. Drew is the lead developer of commonwealth labs maybe, that worked as a contractor for Edgeware but there is no Edgeware lead developer per se, and nobody acting in that capacity that can modify the delivery that were funded without getting to the council or a vote.

> Without requesting any funding, Seedcode also built a beresheet faucet, integrated yieldscan, wrote an ink! tutorial. And dTrade helped build the bridge, which was a major Edgeware milestone

I was unaware of this, and it is not surprising that some of the parts that you developed for dTrade will be useful for Edgeware. It does not complete the contract though, and no settlement has been decided by the council or democracy.

> dTrade founders and team members go beyond Seedcode

This is all fine and dandy, mostly irrelevant though. 

> dTrade did not receive any grants from Edgeware

This is not what is claimed: Seedcode and Drew however worked on dTrade with the treasury funds for the staking UI, which is arguably much worse.

Eventually, I don't think the agency is adequate to comment there, for two reasons: 
1/ The agency should keep a neutral stance wrt contractors. it was not involved with the original proposal, this has been brought of by CW Labs directly.
2/ Some members mentioned that the Seedcode team that was supposed to deal with the staking UI was different from the one working of dTrade, while I showed above that the leads are the same. Although I can accept that those had been mislead in believing this, the facts remain that the agency is not the best entity to comment on something it has not been involved with.

CW Labs could definitely comment if they feel like it, since they brought the team in and were behind the idea of this staking UI for their website, and that some of their members at least, are involved directly with dTrade. But we ought to keep in mind that this would be like asking Philip Morris to comment on the health issues of smoking: they definitely have some knowledge of the topic, but double-checking information is healthy.

@Commonwealth labs, @Edgeware Agency,

could you formulate and post a comprehensive explanation what is going on here?

Happy to further clarify the last bullet point mentioned by Shankar:
- Both the Edgeware lead developer and Seedcode received this grant, and both decided it did not make sense to complete parts of the third milestone
- Without requesting any funding, Seedcode also built a beresheet faucet, integrated yieldscan, wrote an ink! tutorial. And dTrade helped build the bridge, which was a major Edgeware milestone
- dTrade founders and team members go beyond Seedcode
- dTrade did not receive any grants from Edgeware

Interesting points to note here:

• Edgeware being the oldest substrate chain has a collective responsibility to opt stability as Edgeware solochain also has several mainnet deployments.

• Edgeware aims to transition from solochain state to parachain state once WASM & EVM environments can run as flawlessly as they run in solochain state. Thus, launching on Edgeware Parachain might or might not affect dTrade's timeline.

• Edgeware and dTrade have had a very healthy relationship so far. Commonwealth Labs and Edgeware Agency members helped dTrade on several instances in technical, community and development fields. 

• dTrade's founding team Seedcode even got funded from Edgeware Treasury for the 'Staking UI' project which they completely delivered up to 2 milestones and didn't apply for 3rd milestone funding as Seedcode and Drew decided that it was not worth completing.
